text: Throughout the study, the subject also had 3 episodes of Grade 3 TEAEs of headache PT (headache syndrome). The investigator deemed the TEAEs to be related to the study drug, and 2 of the 3 episodes resolved after intramuscular metamizole. The study drug was withdrawn after the 3rd episode, but the subject was followed until the end of the study (EOS) visit. However, the Appendix Table 2.7.4-22 (Figure 9) lists "withdrawal by patient" as the "(r)eason for study drug discontinuation" and the following for the "(r)eason in detail": "The detailed reason is unable to be confirmed."

In the AE narrative, the Applicant reported that the headaches had resolved. In the subject update provided by the Applicant after an Information Request, it was reported that the subject continued to experience severe headaches, which are still ongoing. There are times when the number of episodes can be as high as 5 per week. These episodes are unpredictable and tend to coincide with sudden increases in systolic blood pressure, requiring ad hoc use of sublingual captopril.

Clinical Reviewer's Comment: The subject received two medications during the TEAE of precordial chest pain, and the AE narrative stated that it was "not known" if therapeutic measures were administered. The Applicant's Summary of Clinical Safety reported that the subject's reason for study drug discontinuation was "withdrawal by patient," rather than the recurrent episodes of Grade 3 headache, and that the detailed reason "could not be confirmed," even though the reason was specified at the time of the study drug discontinuation. The AE narrative also stated that the headaches were resolved, even though the subject was followed up to 92 days after the study drug discontinuation (until EOS) and the update stated that these episodes had not resolved and had been frequently recurring.

In Section 1.2.1.1 of CTD Module 2, Section 2.7.4, Summary of Clinical Safety, the Applicant stated that during TP2 the number of subjects discontinued the study drug due to AEs is 5: "(3 [1.2%], 1 [0.8%] and 1 [0.8%] patients, respectively)" in the CT-P43 maintenance, EU-Stelara maintenance, and Switched to CTP43 groups. In the Appendix Table 2.7.4-22 (Figure 9), the Applicant lists the following 3 subjects in the CT-P43 maintenance group for study drug discontinuation due to AEs: (b) (6) for prostatic mass; (b) (6) for hepatitis B surface antigen positivity; and (b) (6) for hepatitis B. The two subjects (b) (6) who discontinued due to Grade 3 headache and Grade 3 "hypersensitivity" headache are not included and said to have discontinued due to "withdrawal by subject" (Figure 9).

In Section 14.3.3 of CTD Module 5.3.5.1, Study CT-P43 3.1 Final Clinical Study report (Figure 10), the Applicant reported that the number of subjects who discontinued the study drug due to AEs is 7 (5 subjects from the CT-P43 maintenance group; 1 from the EU-Stelara maintenance group; and 1 from EU-Stelara – CT-P43 switching group). Among the 5 subjects in the CT-P43 maintenance group, (b) (6) with Grade 3 headache and (b) (6) with fatal myocardial infarction are included, in addition to the 3 subjects mentioned above. The subject (b) (6) with the "hypersensitivity" headache is not included in this total number for either Figure 9 or Figure 10.

Clinical Reviewer's Comment: There is discrepancy in the total numbers and reasons for study drug discontinuation presented in the narratives and tables provided by the Applicant throughout the Application.
